no_junk_drawer_directories.instructions: Does the project structure avoid flat junk-drawer directories that dump many loosely related files or multiple distinct concerns into one folder?

criteria.pass: Directories stay focused and navigable—each folder holds a cohesive set of closely related files or cleanly decomposed feature subfolders rather than a sprawling flat list of unrelated responsibilities. Breaking a complex feature into focused modules or subdirectories is encouraged and does not fail; file count alone or a single ungrouped sub-feature cluster (judged separately under sub-feature grouping) does not make a focused directory a junk drawer.
criteria.fail: Concrete evidence in the manifest shows one or more directories flattening many unrelated responsibilities or distinct concerns into a single crowded folder with genuine ambiguous ownership and navigation cost, rather than grouping them into navigable subfolders. Do not fail based on file count alone or solely by recycling an ungrouped sub-feature cluster from an otherwise focused directory.

cohesive_subfeature_grouping.instructions: Are tightly related file clusters (sharing a domain prefix or importing mostly from each other) grouped into dedicated subfolders instead of sitting flat alongside unrelated peers?

criteria.pass: Multi-file sub-features, component families, or tightly coupled module clusters live together in dedicated subfolders—or stay flat when the entire parent folder is already small and single-purpose. Cleanly decomposing a complex feature into cohesive sub-modules within its own folder passes.
criteria.fail: Concrete evidence in the manifest shows a multi-file cluster (such as several files sharing a sub-feature prefix or forming a tight local-import subgraph) dumped flat into a larger directory alongside unrelated sibling clusters, obscuring ownership.

clear_concern_separation.instructions: Are distinct architectural concerns (such as persistence, external API/transport clients, domain models/rules, UI/presentation, orchestration, and test utilities) cleanly separated rather than mixed flat together?

criteria.pass: Distinct architectural concerns (such as storage/persistence, external clients/transport, core domain logic, UI/presentation, orchestration, and test utilities) are clearly separated by directory or explicit role/naming boundaries (such as distinct `store`, `model`, `transitions`, `client`, `service`, or `view` files within a cohesive feature folder)—whether organized by architectural layer or within cohesive feature folders—without test-only helpers masquerading as production modules.
criteria.fail: Concrete evidence shows multiple unrelated architectural concerns mixed flat in a crowded directory without clear directory or explicit role-naming boundaries (causing ambiguous ownership), OR production-named modules without test scoping/suffixes actually serve only as test utilities alongside production source files. Cohesive feature folders that already separate concerns via explicit role-named files (such as `store`, `model`, `transitions`, `service`, or `client`) do NOT fail.

consistent_organization_depth.instructions: Do similarly sized sibling sub-features within the same parent directory follow a consistent grouping convention, without penalizing modular decomposition of genuinely complex features?

criteria.pass: Comparable, similarly sized sibling clusters within the same parent directory follow a consistent folder organization. Giving a genuinely complex multi-file feature its own subfolder (or nested sub-modules) while smaller one- or two-file siblings remain flat passes cleanly.
criteria.fail: Within the same parent directory, concrete evidence shows one sub-feature extracted into a dedicated subfolder while one or more similarly sized or larger multi-file sibling clusters are left flat in that same parent directory, creating inconsistent navigation.

descriptive_file_roles.instructions: Do file paths and folder names clearly convey ownership without vague catch-all dumping grounds or genuinely ambiguous ownership?

criteria.pass: File paths and folder names make ownership clear. Standard role-named files (such as `service`, `store`, `types`, `model`, `decisions`, `repository`, `validation`, or `routes`) pass when their enclosing directory path cleanly scopes what feature or domain they belong to, even when multiple feature directories use the same role names.
criteria.fail: Concrete evidence shows vague catch-all files (such as `utils`, `helpers`, `common`, `misc`, or un-scoped grab-bag modules) aggregating unrelated responsibilities, or repeated generic names whose enclosing paths fail to distinguish ownership (such as duplicating the same ambiguous file role across overlapping parent and child folders with unclear boundaries).
